name: Congenital Hereditary Endothelial Dystrophy Type II
aliases: Congenital Hereditary Endothelial Dystrophy, Autosomal Recessive

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for CHED2

criteria.description: Bilateral diffuse corneal clouding and edema present at birth or early infancy
Marked reduction or absence of corneal endothelial cells on specular microscopy
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the SLC4A11 gene
Consanguinity or family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
No evidence of intraocular inflammation or secondary causes of corneal edema

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral corneal edema with endothelial cell loss plus identification of pathogenic SLC4A11 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by clinical findings and confirmed by genetic testing; exclusion of other causes of congenital corneal edema is essential.

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC4A11
imaging: Specular microscopy showing decreased or absent corneal endothelial cells
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) demonstrating corneal thickening and edema
genetic: Autosomal recessive mutations in SLC4A11 gene
other: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing diffuse corneal clouding and stromal edema

distinguishingFeatures: Typically adult onset vs congenital in CHED2
Presence of guttae on corneal endothelium
Progressive rather than congenital corneal edema
Presence of central corneal opacity with iridocorneal adhesions

redFlags: Rapidly progressive corneal clouding in infancy
Family history of early-onset corneal edema
references: Vithana EN, Morgan PE, Ramprasad V, et al. SLC4A11 mutations in congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy. Am J Hum Genet. 2006;79(2):354-359.
Mackey DA, Hewitt AW, Hysi PG, et al. Genetic basis of corneal dystrophies. Eye (Lond). 2014;28(2):162-172.
